title: Thin-layer liquid lip color with less repeated amount adjustment

target.statement: Users seeking a thin wearable long-wear liquid color layer who repeatedly remove excess from the applicator. This is a behavior-based research segment; size and willingness to switch are unknown.

objective.statement: Reduce the manual effort needed to obtain the desired thin color layer while preserving an acceptable finish and wear routine. Occasional adjustment is allowed; zero wiping is not a specification.

conditions.statement: Loading should reduce repeated excess removal without requiring more dips or sacrificing even coverage.
Keep the desired thin-layer appearance and wearable result; select actual shade, finish and acceptance targets before testing.
Assess established formula and stock wiper/tip combinations first. Do not assume the observed commercial formula can be copied or a catalogue tip will work unchanged.
Treat gloss-brush pigment cleaning as a separate requirement; a double-ended reservoir does not itself solve it.

tradeoffs.statement: A smaller or more strongly wiped tip could exchange wiping effort for extra dips, uneven coverage or stronger withdrawal force.
Lower applied amount or a formula change could alter coverage, drying, comfort, transfer and wear. The cited study does not establish our formulation.
An existing alternative or a preferred prior tint may be more useful than a new package. Reported shade and touch-up preferences are separate from loading inconvenience.

failure_modes.statement: Variable loading with fill level, handling, viscosity or accumulated residue could erase the convenience gain.
Tight wiping could leave end droplets, damage flock, increase withdrawal force or require extra dipping.
An easier-to-load package could still produce patchy color, poor wear or uncomfortable film.
Solvent, seal, adhesive or material incompatibility could make a stock pack unsuitable.

falsifiers: Retire the new-product premise if an acceptable available alternative achieves the desired result with an ordinary routine the target user accepts.
Reject a package revision if it reduces removed mass but fails to reduce total effort, adds dips, or worsens the chosen coverage/wear result.
Reframe or stop if shade, finish, retouching or price dominates the amount-control benefit, or no practical compatible stock combination exists.
boundaries: This is a conditional development concept, not demonstrated market absence or a validated formula.
No concentrations, dose targets, proprietary recipe, novel resin, patent clearance, MOQ, manufacturing cost or regulatory qualification are specified.
No prototype, purchase, outreach, human trial or laboratory measurement has occurred.
